adapters.rationale: Rule-based SAST that scans in seconds and accepts repository-specific rules. Weakest on cross-function logic flaws.
High-precision dependency scanning against the OSV database; fast and low-noise enough to run as a per-change gate.
Breadth in one binary: dependencies, container images, IaC, secrets, licences. Better as a scheduled sweep than a per-change gate.
History-aware secret detection. Complements the built-in fitness rule, which only sees the current working tree.
Produces the artifact inventory (SBOM) that later vulnerability rescans and provenance attestation depend on.
Detects personal data in text and structured data. Its own docs state it cannot find everything; treat it as one layer, not a boundary.
Measures whether the tests would actually catch a defect. Run per change with incremental mode; a nightly-only signal arrives after the merge.
Generates adversarial requests from the API schema, covering inputs no hand-written case would include.
Asserts latency and error-rate objectives under load. Its result describes a deployed system, not the current diff.
Infrastructure misconfiguration is where availability and security failures usually originate rather than in application code.
Validates service level objectives declared as code so the availability target is reviewable and machine-readable.
